/padel-praha/.title: Padel in Prague: clubs, prices and booking
/padel-praha/.description: Compare 18 padel clubs in Prague and nearby. Explore prices, indoor courts, MultiSport and places for your first game, with links to available times.
/padel-praha/.intro: Our catalog covers 18 clubs in Prague and nearby. For a first game, look for rental equipment and possibly a lesson; for regular doubles, compare a shared playing time, the journey and the cost. We search availability for today and the next seven days, and you complete your booking with the club.

sections.heading: Choose a venue, then a time
sections.body: For winter play, start with the indoor overview. If budget matters most, compare the full hourly tariff rather than just the lowest advertised price. Open availability on the club profile; complete booking and payment with the operator.

sections.heading: How to read the comparison
sections.body: The catalog also includes Vestec and Jinočany outside Prague. At a mixed venue, the total court count is not the number of indoor courts. MultiSport acceptance alone does not establish your supplement. A source-check date applies only to the facts explicitly listed as checked.

sections.heading: Choosing a club for an after-work game
sections.body:
Imagine four players planning a weekday evening game. One travels from Smíchov, another from Zličín and two from offices in the centre. Agree on the latest acceptable start, then compare everyone’s journey to two or three clubs. The court nearest the organizer may leave the rest of the group with a difficult trip.

Next, compare the same playing time and duration. If you need rackets, add rental to the budget and confirm that equipment is available before paying for the court.
items: Agree on a day, session length and two acceptable start times.
Compare the whole group’s journey, court cover and total cost.
Complete the club’s booking and share its confirmation.

/padel-praha-ceny/.title: Prague padel prices 2026: club comparison
/padel-praha-ceny/.description: Hourly padel prices at 18 clubs in Prague and nearby. Time bands, court types, MultiSport, sources and clearly marked unverified information.
/padel-praha-ceny/.intro: The price usually covers a whole court for one hour, not one player. For example, Padel Powers publishes 800 CZK on weekdays before 16:00 and 900 CZK in the evening and at weekends. Below we also show older catalog tariffs that have not been checked again.

sections.heading: Compare the same duration and format
sections.body: Compare an hour of doubles with an hour of doubles. The Court has a separate tariff for its 1vs1 training court; its minimum is therefore not the standard-court price. Compare a 90-minute game by its final booking total, rather than automatically multiplying an advertised starting price.

sections.heading: What can change the total
sections.body: Evening time bands, season, membership and equipment rental can change your final payment. Neride's winter tariff applies from 1 October 2026 to 30 April 2027. Keep MultiSport credits separate from the amount you must pay upfront.

sections.heading: Price comparison methodology
sections.body: Each verified price list has its own check date and official source link. Checked standard-court rates are summarized separately from unverified catalog values. An unknown price is not zero, and checking a price list does not confirm every club service. Confirm the final price for your actual slot before paying.

sections.heading: What a 100 CZK court-price difference means
sections.body:
At Padel Powers’ published rates of 800 and 900 CZK, the difference for four players is 25 CZK each per hour. That saving may not justify changing everyone’s schedule or travelling across the city. If you play regularly, compare several workable times and calculate a monthly budget using the number of visits you actually plan.

The lowest rate in the table is a starting point. Base your decision on the amount for your court, playing time and booking length.
items: Select a standard court and the same interval at both clubs.
Add the equipment you need to rent.
Divide the final amount by the number of paying players.

/padel-praha-multisport/.title: Padel with MultiSport in Prague: clubs and terms
/padel-praha-multisport/.description: Where to use MultiSport for padel in Prague. Compare documented terms, credit, supplements and other clubs with unverified card acceptance.
/padel-praha-multisport/.intro: MultiSport does not automatically mean a whole court without payment. The number of cards, playing time and reimbursement method matter. At One Padel, reimbursement takes the form of club credit for a later visit.

sections.heading: One Padel: credit and conflicting amounts
sections.body: From 1 October 2026, the club describes up to four cards per booking. For daytime play it lists both 222 and 222.50 CZK per card and a total of 888 CZK. We therefore do not promise an exact supplement or free play. Ask the club to confirm credit for your time. Digital cards can be used at self-service check-in; plastic cards are checked at reception with ID.

sections.heading: Supplement, credit or payment on site
sections.body:
Neride lists card acceptance without a verified supplement. Plechovka lists 25% of the court covered per card and a 25 CZK supplement per player. Radotín and LTC Modřany return a share of the first hour as credit after payment.

Císařská louka requires on-site card use and does not apply it retrospectively to online payments. Satalice requires a phone booking for MultiSport. Each model therefore needs a different booking process.

sections.heading: Five questions before booking
sections.body: Confirm card eligibility for your time, the maximum number of cards, the full booking price, reimbursement and cancellation. Also ask whether the card is applied before payment, on arrival or after play. Club credit is not the same as money refunded to your bank account.

sections.heading: When only two of four players have a card
sections.body:
Two cards in a group of four do not automatically halve the bill. The club decides which part of the booking is covered and whether to deduct it immediately or return it as credit. The organizer may need to pay for the whole court before any credit is added after card check-in.

Agree how to share that credit too. If it stays in the booking player’s account, everyone should understand how it affects the group’s settlement.
items: Tell the club how many cardholders will actually attend.
Ask for the amount due now and how each card must be presented.
Agree who keeps the credit and how to settle it within the group.

/kryty-padel-praha/.title: Indoor padel in Prague: courts for winter play
/kryty-padel-praha/.description: Indoor padel courts in Prague and nearby. Compare halls, court counts, hourly prices and availability before making your winter booking.
/kryty-padel-praha/.intro: For winter padel, choose a specific covered court. The catalog includes fully indoor and mixed venues. A club's name or total court count alone does not tell you how many courts are currently indoors.

sections.heading: Large halls and a smaller training venue
sections.body: One Padel lists nine indoor courts, and Padel Powers eight. The Court has two standard courts and one training court under a roof. In Hostivař, Džus offers four indoor courts. These are different options for groups and individual practice, not a ranking of quality.

sections.heading: Check heating and operation separately
sections.body: Neride describes a heated hall on its website. For other venues we do not confirm a specific temperature or year-round availability of every court. Seasonal covers, maintenance closures and opening hours can change; open the club's booking system before travelling.

sections.heading: Choosing a winter time
sections.body: First compare the journey and price for your preferred hour, then available times. Two groups of four playing simultaneously need two courts for the same interval. The venue's court count alone does not guarantee that availability.

sections.heading: Two available courts may not give you a shared game
sections.body:
Suppose one indoor court is free from 18:00 to 19:00 and another from 19:00 to 20:00. That does not work for eight players who want to start together. You need two standard courts with matching start and end times; a 1vs1 training court cannot accommodate the second doubles group.

Once you find a shared interval, check both courts in the club’s system. Treat the time as a proposal until both bookings are confirmed.
items: Check that each selected court is indoors.
For eight players, find two standard courts over the same interval.
Confirm the winter rate and both bookings with the club.

/padel-praha-podle-lokalit/.title: Where to play padel in Prague by location
/padel-praha-podle-lokalit/.description: Padel in Smíchov, Hostivař, Radotín and other parts of Prague. Clubs grouped by address in one overview, with links to prices and booking.
/padel-praha-podle-lokalit/.intro: Start with the part of Prague everyone can reach comfortably. Smíchov, Zličín, Hostivař and Radotín offer different options; the catalog also includes nearby towns such as Jinočany and Vestec. Check the address and route for your actual playing time.

sections.heading: Prague 5 and the western surroundings
sections.body: Smíchov has Padel Powers and Císařská louka. Zličín has One Padel, and west of the city Jinočany has The Court. These are different locations and court types, so check the specific address and route before choosing.

sections.heading: Prague 15 and 16
sections.body: In Prague 15 you will find Neride and Džus in the Hostivař area. Radotín has Padel Radotín and Padel Hall Olympia Radotín. We have not verified precise journey times, parking availability or public-transport connections; plan these for the actual day and hour.

sections.heading: Use the address when arranging where to meet
sections.body:
Send the club’s name and full address when arranging a game. “Padel in Radotín” is ambiguous because the catalog includes both Padel Radotín and Padel Hall Olympia Radotín. Smíchov and Zličín are also different destinations, even though both are on Prague’s western side.

If some players drive and others use public transport, compare both journeys. Include the trip home after an evening game and time to change; distance from home alone does not cover either.
items: Share the exact club name and address.
Check the outward and return journeys for the actual day and time.
Agree to meet before the paid court session begins.

/blog/kolik-stoji-padel-praha/.title: How much does your first padel game in Prague cost?
/blog/kolik-stoji-padel-praha/.description: Work out padel costs for four players: court hire, racket rental and playing time. A Padel Powers price example and links to the club comparison.
/blog/kolik-stoji-padel-praha/.intro: For doubles, divide the whole-court price between four players. An 800 CZK hour at Padel Powers works out at 200 CZK each, or 225 CZK each for an evening hour at 900 CZK. Budget separately for equipment and other services.

sections.heading: Example budget for your first hour
sections.body: If all four players need a racket and reception confirms a 50 CZK rental per person for your game, the daytime hour works out at 250 CZK per player. This is a calculation from the club's price list, not a package or HLEDEJKURTY offer. It does not include balls or a coach.

sections.heading: Watch starting prices and singles courts
sections.body:
The Court separates standard-court and training-court prices. Do not compare the lower 1vs1 tariff with a court for four players.

A longer booking may cross two price bands; the final total in the booking system is what matters.

sections.heading: How to keep costs sensible
sections.body: Compare several times, agree how to split costs and check equipment in advance. MultiSport may mean credit for next time rather than a smaller upfront payment. The prices page provides the full tariff comparison; this article focuses on one group's budget.

sections.heading: Four players with their own equipment
sections.body:
With four paying players and your own equipment, divide the court charge by four. If one person drops out and the others pay for the same court, divide by three: 800 CZK becomes about 267 CZK each.

Compare per-player costs using the same group size. These calculations are not club packages or offers of individual places.

sections.heading: Add racket rental separately
sections.body:
Džus lists a racket at 50 CZK per game. Four rented rackets therefore add 200 CZK to this example, or 50 CZK per person. Using its published daytime rate of 800 CZK for one court-hour, the court and four rackets total 1,000 CZK, or 250 CZK per player.

Balls, travel and any coach are excluded. Confirm the number of available rackets and the rental charge for your actual session before paying.

sections.heading: Longer play across a peak-rate boundary
sections.body:
For example, a weekday standard court at The Court from 12:00 to 14:00 crosses the 800 CZK band before 13:00 and the 1,000 CZK band after 13:00. When priced by those hourly bands, the total is 1,800 CZK, or 450 CZK each for four players, excluding equipment. Multiplying the lowest rate by two would be misleading.

For 90 minutes, read the price of the actual slot; the booking system may use its own reservation blocks and cancellation terms.

sections.heading: Who pays when the group changes?
sections.body:
Before booking, agree whether the organizer collects everyone’s share in advance or after the game. If someone drops out, check the cancellation deadline and try to find a replacement. Splitting the bill among the remaining players is your group’s decision; fewer players do not necessarily reduce the club’s court charge.

If only some players use MultiSport, separate the shared payment from any credit added to a player account. Otherwise, the bill can appear settled even though only the booking player received the contribution.
items: Check the final price and cancellation terms before paying.
Agree when shares are due and what happens after a withdrawal.
Keep rental charges and any club credit separate from court hire.

/blog/multisport-padel-jak-rezervovat/.title: Padel and MultiSport: what to check before booking
/blog/multisport-padel-jak-rezervovat/.description: A practical guide to booking padel with MultiSport. Understand upfront payment, supplements, club credit, card check-in and cancellation terms.
/blog/multisport-padel-jak-rezervovat/.intro: Find out how the club applies your card before paying for a booking. A MultiSport label alone does not tell you what the game will cost or when your contribution will be returned.

sections.heading: Agree how many cards your group has
sections.body: Each player should check their own card and the club's identification requirements. Do not assume one card covers all four players. Terms may depend on the playing hour and the number of cardholders who attend.

sections.heading: A club-wallet example
sections.body:
One Padel describes reimbursement as wallet credit. Distinguish the amount payable now from credit usable later.

Confirm the exact value with the club: its published text gives conflicting amounts for the daytime band.

sections.heading: Before arrival and when cancelling
sections.body: Check check-in time, where to scan the card and the cancellation deadline. After playing, check that credit was added. If someone does not attend, do not assume the same discount. The MultiSport comparison page lists clubs and sources.

sections.heading: A message you can send to the club
sections.body:
For example: “We want a standard court for four players for one hour, and two of us have MultiSport. What do we pay when booking, when do you scan the cards, and whose account receives any credit?” Add your actual date and time. This separates the reservation payment from a contribution usable on a later visit.

If a cardholder drops out after you receive an answer, contact the club before playing. The original calculation may no longer apply to your group.
items: Count the cards and choose a specific session.
Confirm payment, card check-in and any credit.
Read cancellation terms before paying and check the settlement afterwards.

/blog/padel-v-zime-praha/.title: Winter padel in Prague: choosing a hall and time
/blog/padel-v-zime-praha/.description: Plan winter padel in Prague step by step. Choose an indoor court, check seasonal prices and equipment, and find a shared time for one or two groups.
/blog/padel-v-zime-praha/.intro: In winter, start by checking the cover of your specific court and the winter tariff. Mixed venues can list both indoor and outdoor courts in the same booking system.

sections.heading: Choose a court that is actually covered
sections.body: One Padel and Padel Powers describe indoor venues; The Court describes two standard and one training court under a roof. At mixed venues, check the individual court label. A photograph or the word Hall in the name alone does not confirm current cover.

sections.heading: Winter prices may differ from summer prices
sections.body: For 1 October 2026–30 April 2027, Neride lists 690 CZK outside the evening peak and 820 CZK on weekdays from 16:00 to 24:00. Do not use the old summer list to estimate a winter payment.

sections.heading: Make a shared plan
sections.body: Agree arrival time, equipment and how to split costs. For two groups of four, select two courts in the finder. If your chosen time disappears, try another start time or club; our saved availability does not hold a court for you.

sections.heading: Agree on a backup start time
sections.body:
Suppose four of you want an evening game indoors but could also start later. Compare both times in advance and agree on a backup together. If the first slot disappears while you move to the booking system, you can use the alternative without contacting everyone again.

Pack dry sportswear and footwear permitted by the club. If renting, confirm where to collect equipment, especially outside normal reception hours. An indoor court does not itself confirm that reception will be open.
items: Agree on a preferred and backup time with everyone.
Check the court cover and winter-season price.
Confirm venue access and where to collect rented rackets.

/blog/padel-pro-zacatecniky-praha/.title: Padel for beginners in Prague: your first game
/blog/padel-pro-zacatecniky-praha/.description: Prepare for your first padel game in Prague: four players, racket rental, lessons, basic rules and booking, with checked examples of local clubs.
/blog/padel-pro-zacatecniky-praha/.intro: You do not need to buy a racket straight away for your first game. First choose a club with equipment rental and decide whether you want an introductory lesson or a friendly doubles game of your own.

sections.heading: Agree the format and equipment
sections.body: Plan standard doubles for four players of a similar level. Bring sportswear, water and shoes that meet the venue's surface rules. Padel Powers and One Padel offer equipment rental; confirm availability of four rackets in advance.

sections.heading: A lesson or your own first match
sections.body: A coach can explain serving, movement as a pair and safe play near the glass. Padel Powers, One Padel and Džus publish lessons. Ask whether the price includes the court and equipment, how many people it covers and whether it is suitable for complete beginners.

sections.heading: Arrive with a booking and a simple aim
sections.body: After choosing an available time, complete the booking with the club and read the confirmation. Warm up before play, use the racket's safety strap and start with slow rallies. Before your first set, agree how you will score and handle deuce.

sections.heading: What to do during your first game together
sections.body:
Start with gentle rallies and give everyone a chance to try serving. An aim could be to keep the ball in play and learn how it rebounds from the glass. If a rule becomes confusing, stop before the next point and talk through that situation; repeatedly guessing the score uses up your booked time.

Only two players available? Adjust the plan before paying: invite another pair, look for an open game or ask about a lesson or a dedicated 1vs1 training court. Booking a doubles court does not supply the missing players.
items: Confirm the player count and any rented rackets.
Explain serving and scoring before the first point.
If you want coaching, explicitly book a lesson.

/blog/pravidla-padelu/.title: Padel rules made simple: serving and scoring
/blog/pravidla-padelu/.description: A beginner's guide to padel rules based on FIP 2026. Underarm serving, glass walls, two bounces and a scoring example with different deuce formats.
/blog/pravidla-padelu/.intro: For your first doubles game, understand serving, bounces and scoring. This summary follows International Padel Federation rules effective from 1 January 2026; competitions are governed by the full rules and their announced format.

sections.heading: How to serve
sections.body: The server lets the ball bounce and hits it at or below waist height. Serve diagonally into the opposite service box, starting from the right, with two attempts. The receiver must let the serve bounce. A serve that lands in the correct box and then hits the metal fence before its second bounce is a fault.

sections.heading: Glass and the end of a rally
sections.body:
During a rally, you may volley the ball. If it reaches an opponent’s wall, it must bounce in their court before touching that wall. After rebounding off your own glass, you can return it before its second ground bounce.

Two bounces on your side lose the point. The fence has separate rules; do not treat it as glass. Returning serve is different: the serve must bounce first.

sections.heading: A scoring example and a pre-match agreement
sections.body:
Regular points run 0, 15, 30, 40, game. At 30:15, a point for the receiving pair makes it 30:30. For a recreational match you can agree on traditional advantage at deuce; the 2026 rules also contain alternative systems. Six games with a two-game lead usually win a set, with a tie-break commonly played at 6:6.

Check the competition's format before entering.

sections.heading: Reading the serve diagram
sections.body:
Point 1 represents the server behind the service line on the right side of their half. Point 2 is the opposite service box across the net: the first serve must land there. Bounce the ball on the ground before hitting it, and strike no higher than waist level.

The diagram shows the serve direction, not all four players or every foot-position requirement. Alternate serving sides after each point. The receiver must let the serve bounce before returning it.

sections.heading: Three common beginner disputes
sections.body: First distinguish a serve from an ongoing rally. These situations have different outcomes. In a friendly game, stop and clarify a disputed rule before the next point.
items: During a rally, the ball bounces in the opponents’ court and then hits the glass: play continues.
The ball hits the opponents’ glass directly without first bouncing in their court: the attacking pair loses the point.
A serve lands correctly but hits the metal fence before its second bounce: a service fault. During a regular rally that fence rebound can be valid.

sections.heading: Practise scoring without an argument
sections.body:
In a recreational game using traditional advantage, imagine the serving pair wins a point at 40:40. They have advantage. Winning the next point gives them the game; losing it returns the score to deuce. This example assumes you agreed to traditional advantage, since another announced deuce format may work differently.

Call the score before each serve, giving the serving pair’s points first. This also helps everyone follow the move between right and left service positions.
items: Agree on the deuce format and how the set ends before starting.
Let the serve bounce before returning it.
Judge a disputed rebound according to whether it was a serve or a rally.

/blog/padel-tenis-squash/.title: Padel, tennis and squash: which should you try first?
/blog/padel-tenis-squash/.description: A practical first-visit comparison of padel, tennis and squash: players, walls, equipment and choosing a suitable game format in Prague.
/blog/padel-tenis-squash/.intro: All three sports use rackets, but court booking and play differ. Start with how many people you have and whether you want a game across a net or against a front wall.

sections.heading: Padel: four players and walls
sections.body: Standard padel doubles uses a court divided by a net, with walls coming into play after a bounce. If you come from tennis, do not automatically transfer your serving habits or out calls. For two players, look explicitly for a 1vs1 format, such as The Court's training court.

sections.heading: Choose tennis and squash separately
sections.body: Tennis offers singles and doubles across a net. Squash is normally played by two people against a front wall, with its own scoring and interference rules. HLEDEJKURTY compares padel times in this overview, so confirm availability for other sports directly with the venue.

sections.heading: A first visit without unnecessary purchases
sections.body: Rent the correct racket for each sport and check permitted footwear. A padel rental service does not necessarily rent squash equipment. Before paying, check the booking duration and whole-court price. For padel, the Prague club overview can help you choose.

sections.heading: Choose around the players who will actually attend
sections.body:
For four people wanting to play together, compare padel doubles with tennis doubles. For two, consider tennis singles, squash or an explicitly offered padel 1vs1 format. Choosing around your actual group avoids paying for a court and only then trying to recruit more people.

On a first visit, ask for the rules of that particular sport. A wall rebound in padel and play against the front wall in squash serve different purposes; experience in one game does not explain the other.
items: Count how many people want to play at once.
Check the sport, court format and equipment in the booking.
Compare costs for the same duration and player count.

/blog/spoluhraci-padel-praha/.title: How to find a fourth padel player in Prague
/blog/spoluhraci-padel-praha/.description: Find padel partners in Prague through One Padel and Džus open games. Agree on level, split the cost and confirm bookings without misunderstandings.
/blog/spoluhraci-padel-praha/.intro: Missing one player? Start with open games in club systems. One Padel lists them on its website, and Džus describes them among its booking-system features.

sections.heading: Open games have their own terms
sections.body: An open game is more than an available court: it offers places in a particular group. Check the level, time, duration and per-player price. At One Padel, open the games section; at Džus, look in Bookaball. HLEDEJKURTY itself does not match players.

sections.heading: Include the information people need
sections.body: State the date, time, club, duration, approximate level and share of the price. For example: Looking for a fourth player for a friendly one-hour indoor game; price and booking to be confirmed once the group is complete. Share personal contact details only where needed and follow the community group's rules.

sections.heading: Who pays and who can cancel?
sections.body: Before paying, agree on an organizer, cost-sharing and what happens if someone drops out. Share the confirmed booking with the group, not just a time found in the availability search. If you need to choose a club first, compare journeys and prices in the Prague overview.

sections.heading: Describe your level without relying on a number
sections.body:
Instead of saying only “beginner,” explain what you can do. For example: “We can serve but are still learning to use the glass. We want a friendly hour, not a competitive match.” This is a sample message, not a real game listing. Add the date, club and price once confirmed.

When joining an existing open game, ask the organizer whether that experience fits the group. Shared expectations help more than an unexplained level label.
items: Include the date, time, duration, venue and price or how it will be confirmed.
Describe your experience and whether you want friendly or competitive play.
Agree who organizes and what happens if someone withdraws.

/blog/jak-vybrat-padelovy-klub-praha/.title: How to choose a padel club in Prague for your game
/blog/jak-vybrat-padelovy-klub-praha/.description: Choose a padel club for your needs: a first lesson, several courts, 1vs1 play or price. Transparent criteria and specific Prague examples.
/blog/jak-vybrat-padelovy-klub-praha/.intro: Choose around the game you are planning: an introductory lesson needs an available coach and equipment, while two doubles groups need two standard courts at the same time. These suggestions use club websites and the catalog. They do not replace a visit or a hands-on assessment of playing conditions.

sections.heading: For a first game or lesson
sections.body: Check equipment rental, available introductory lessons and a format suitable for your group. One Padel and Padel Powers list both rental and coaches. That does not mean rental equipment or lessons will be available without a reservation at your chosen time.

sections.heading: For several groups or two players
sections.body: One Padel's website lists nine indoor courts, and Padel Powers eight. For several groups of four, confirm a shared time interval. If two of you want 1vs1 play, The Court lists a separate training court. The overall court count does not guarantee availability.

sections.heading: For your budget and journey
sections.body: Compare the same hour at several clubs and include equipment in the final price. We do not judge clubs by marketing adjectives. Families should check specific facilities and supervision; a children's corner does not mean childcare. Plan transport using the real address and a current route.

sections.heading: Different groups need different choices
sections.body:
For two people wanting 1vs1 practice, The Court’s separate training court is a specific option. For eight players in two doubles groups, look for two standard courts at the same time. The indoor court counts at One Padel and Padel Powers make them candidates, but you still need to check that shared interval.

For each candidate, note one deciding requirement, such as an available lesson or a workable journey. If the club cannot meet it at your chosen time, a longer facilities list does not solve the problem.
items: Choose one requirement without which the game cannot go ahead.
Compare two or three clubs for the same session.
Check the total price and confirm the service you need.

/blog/padel-lekce-treneri-praha/.title: Padel lessons and coaches in Prague: how to choose
/blog/padel-lekce-treneri-praha/.description: Prague padel clubs that advertise lessons, and how to compare coaching. Individual or group training, equipment and whether court hire is included.
/blog/padel-lekce-treneri-praha/.intro: Clubs advertising lessons include One Padel, Padel Powers, Džus and Neride. First decide whether you want an introduction, a session for your group of four or individual technique work.

sections.heading: Ask for the full price
sections.body: Compare the number of players, duration and whether the court and racket are included. Neride publishes prices for different group sizes with a hall and coach; another club may quote a particular lesson format. The same amount may therefore cover a different service.

sections.heading: Choose a level and language
sections.body: Tell the coach your experience, group size, preferred language and main goal. A beginner group and competition preparation need different content. One Padel explicitly lists individual and group lessons for children and adults; check its current schedule with the club.

sections.heading: What to confirm before your first lesson
sections.body: Ask about the meeting point, equipment and cancellation terms. An ordinary court booking does not book a coach. HLEDEJKURTY can help with court availability; the club or coach confirms the coaching and its price.

sections.heading: An enquiry for a first group lesson
sections.body:
You could write: “We are four adults with no padel experience. We want an introductory lesson covering serving, scoring and movement as a pair. We need rented rackets; please quote the total including the court and confirm the teaching language.” Add possible dates. This gives the coach enough information to propose a suitable format.

For a later lesson, describe one situation you struggle with, such as returning a ball after it hits the glass. A specific goal is easier to plan around than wanting to improve everything at once.
items: State the player count, experience, language and lesson goal.
Ask for the total price and what it includes.
Confirm both the coach and court and read the cancellation terms.

/blog/padel-firmy-teambuilding-praha/.title: Corporate padel in Prague: planning a team event
/blog/padel-firmy-teambuilding-praha/.description: Plan a corporate padel event in Prague: court numbers, beginners, coaching, refreshments and a confirmed quote, with examples of clubs for groups.
/blog/padel-firmy-teambuilding-praha/.intro: A corporate event needs more than a few separate court bookings. Confirm the participant count, court rotation, equipment and responsibility for the full program with the club.

sections.heading: Turn player numbers into a playing plan
sections.body: Standard doubles needs four players per court. Twelve people playing simultaneously therefore need three courts. If groups rotate, plan activities while they wait and an approximate timetable; not everyone may want to compete throughout.

sections.heading: Choose for facilities and your team's experience
sections.body: The Court advertises corporate evenings and tournaments. Padel Powers has eight indoor courts and a meeting room; One Padel has nine indoor courts and a lounge. These are reasons to make an enquiry, not confirmation of event capacity or a package price.

sections.heading: Request one written quote
sections.body: Include courts, coaching, rackets, balls, refreshments, invoicing and cancellation in the quote. State how many complete beginners are attending. Available courts found in the search are not a confirmed corporate program; agree a group event directly with the operator.

sections.heading: An example plan for twelve colleagues
sections.body:
Twelve people can play simultaneously on three standard courts. On two courts, eight play while four wait, so you need an agreed rotation. If there are complete beginners, allow time to explain the rules and tell the coach how many people will attend; introductory teaching uses part of the playing time.

Separate the sporting programme from the space you want afterwards. A meeting room or lounge in the facilities list does not mean it is included in your price or reserved exclusively for your team.

/blog/padel-turnaje-praha/.title: Padel tournaments in Prague: where to find dates
/blog/padel-turnaje-praha/.description: Find current padel tournaments and club calendars in Prague. Check the level, partner requirements, entry fee and registration before signing up.
/blog/padel-turnaje-praha/.intro: Find current padel tournaments in the calendars at One Padel, Padel Powers and Džus; check federation competitions with the Czech Padel Federation. Before entering, establish the category, format and entry-fee terms. An available court is not a tournament registration.

sections.heading: Start with the official club calendar
sections.body: One Padel has a tournament section, Džus publishes events, and Padel Powers lists club events and tournaments. For each listing, check the date, location, spaces and registration deadline. For federation competitions, also check Czech Padel Federation requirements.

sections.heading: Tournaments suit different levels
sections.body: Read the category description and format. Some events require a pair, while others accept individuals and rotate partners. Interpret beginner labels or level letters using that organizer's explanation; they may mean different things at different clubs.

sections.heading: What to pay and confirm
sections.body: Before paying, check whether the entry fee is per person or pair, what it includes and how withdrawals work. An ordinary court-booking confirmation does not replace tournament registration. For your own preparation, choose a training time on the club profiles.

sections.heading: Entering alone when the event requires a pair
sections.body:
First check whether the organizer accepts individuals or needs your partner’s name when you register. At a pairs event, an available place on the participant list is not itself an offer of a partner. Ask whether you can add a partner later and when your lineup must be confirmed.

For a first tournament, ask about both the category and the full day’s schedule. Your first match time does not tell you when the event ends; ask when your last game could finish under the programme.
